flags.observation: "Confession:" is spoken as a label; the sentence after it is a self-introduction, not a confession.
Style B specifies a female lead, but the narrator says "I'm Uncle FrizzleBob"; voice and narrator clash in variant B.
Dog whistles are announced ("Insiders, listen for") and all three names recur in card lines, so experts get no hidden reward.
"stop rogue trading and failures": after the cut, failures dangles with no object; heard once, the phrase is unclear.
"Meanwhile" is a parallel, and-then bridge, not a therefore/but link out of the Kean card.
"Circled:" then "So, herd the deer" builds a frame-made causal chain from the PNAC quote straight into the Wedge One deaths.
"just moved back in" has no subject; the listener cannot tell who moved before hearing who was killed.
"largest accounting fraud in history, then Secretary of the Army" drops his Enron executive role; it reads as White being the fraud.
"Rumsfeld's war" without its target (the bureaucracy) reads as a shooting war; the card's meaning shifts.
Power recited as a fact: "fifteen years falsifying Navy records" takes half the line and is stated about a named real person.
"changed everything? Right:" has lost its subject; the verdict's setup does not land when heard once.
"Guess who pays for both." is a stock tag that could close any money satire.
